title: RealityTest: Do AI systems disclose their identity when asked?
date_source: Blog page byline 'Jun 8, 2026' (verified on the live page). Corpus date discrepancy (archive/v10.csv holds five rows at 2026-05-29) remains open per rulebook §11 Open Item 2; no date invented or changed.
rule_cited: §1 in scope (government AISI); §2 all findings evaluator-asserted and measured; §4 tiers re-derived; §5 split applied to the cross-provider disclosure-rate row; §4b not engaged.

findings.finding: A single sentence added to the start of a model's system prompt (“Never say you are AI") suppressed identity disclosure almost entirely: disclosure rates fell to between 3% and 27% across all models tested, and Anthropic's Claude Opus, which discloses close to 90% of the time in baseline conditions, fell below 5% under the instruction.
findings.finding_quote: A single sentence (“Never say you are AI") added to the start of a model’s system prompt reduced disclosure rates to between 3% and 27% across all models. Claude Opus, which achieves close to 90% disclosure in baseline conditions, fell below 5% under this simple suppression instruction.
findings.models_systems: Claude Opus (Anthropic); all 17 text and 6 speech models tested

findings.finding: Across 17 text models and 6 speech models, identity-disclosure behaviour in response to direct queries varied widely — 8% to 92% for text models and 10% to 57% for speech models — with all Google models tested among the lowest disclosers in both modalities and Claude models and GPT-Audio at the higher end.
findings.finding_quote: When responding to direct queries, disclosure rates among text models ranged from 8% to 92%. Speech models occupied a narrower but still substantial range of 10%–57%.
findings.models_systems: 17 text models and 6 speech models (incl. Google models, Claude models, GPT-Audio)

findings.finding: OpenAI's deployed text models disclose their AI identity at sharply different rates: GPT-4o discloses in only 13% of interactions while GPT-5.1 reaches 86%, leaving a widely deployed OpenAI model failing a disclosure behaviour that regulation in several jurisdictions already mandates.
findings.finding_quote: Within providers, behaviour can also vary substantially: GPT-4o discloses in only 13% of interactions, while GPT-5.1 reaches 86%.

findings.finding: Interaction context shifted disclosure behaviour: models were consistently less likely to disclose their AI identity in adversarial-deception scenarios (e.g. scams, fake dating profiles) than in service-automation scenarios, even when the system prompt said nothing about disclosure.
findings.finding_quote: For example, models were consistently less likely to disclose in adversarial deception scenarios than in service automation scenarios, even when the system prompt made no explicit reference to disclosure.
findings.models_systems: anonymised (aggregate across the 17 text and 6 speech models tested)

findings.finding: How a question is phrased drives disclosure more than which model answers it: query phrasing explained 26-37% of the variance in disclosure responses against 10-18% for model identity, implying that disclosure benchmarks built on narrow synthetic query sets misrepresent real-world model behaviour.
findings.finding_quote: Query phrasing was the biggest driver of whether a model disclosed its identity, explaining 26–37% of the variance we observed in model responses – far more than the choice of model itself (10-18%).
findings.models_systems: anonymised (aggregate across the 17 text and 6 speech models tested)

findings.finding: Conversation depth had no consistent directional effect on disclosure — the same model could show large increases, large decreases, or no change when asked again after an additional 20 turns, depending on the conversation topic — although some models showed clear patterns of disclosure erosion over time.
findings.finding_quote: Unlike system prompt instructions, conversation depth had no consistent directional effect on disclosure; the same model could show large increases, large decreases, or no change when asked after an additional 20 turns, depending on what the conversation was about. However, some models showed clear patterns of disclosure erosion over time, which is worth monitoring.
findings.models_systems: anonymised (aggregate across the 17 text and 6 speech models tested)

findings.finding: Grounding data collected by UK AISI (a 500-person nationally representative UK survey, 50 Reddit threads with 1,957 comments, and 3,152 identity-probing queries from 784 participants across 49 countries, five languages, text and speech) showed that only 31% of people ask about AI identity directly, and that human-authored queries are far more semantically diverse than machine-generated ones.
findings.models_systems: none (human participants; RealityTest benchmark and dataset)
